clue.text: Coach constrained back causing fracas

parts.note: a coach is a long-distance bus

indicators.note: back asks for the word meaning constrained to be read from its end towards its start

parts.note: put as in hard put, forced or pressed by circumstances

explanation.surface: A sports coach, held back from the touchline, provokes a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: Constrained reads as put in the sense of hard put, forced by circumstances; the coach is a vehicle, not a trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust-up is a noisy quarrel or brawl, the same as a fracas.

clue.text: End of Big Bertha's dins reverberating? Bikini followed it much later (12, two words)

indicators.note: sounds reverberating bounce about, so these letters are thrown into a new order
end of says to keep only the final letter of the next word

parts.note: the last letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: The roar of the Big Bertha howitzer in the Great War, with Bikini Atoll's bomb tests decades later.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Bertha and Bikini both summon weapons, but the Bikini here is the swimsuit, which arrived long after the modest one-piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathing dress was the full-cover women's swimming costume that the two-piece bikini replaced in the mid twentieth century.

clue.text: Paul's excited about teaching of religion increasing

indicators.note: about means the mixed letters go round the next piece
something excited is stirred up, so the name's letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
RI is religious instruction, the old school subject

explanation.surface: Paul gets worked up over the growing teaching of religion.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, was the British school name for religious education.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprisal is a rare word for a rising up, and the definition reads as a noun: an increase.

clue.text: Bone: start of problem cutting more than one saddle up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for saddles reads from bottom to top
a letter cutting a word is set inside it

parts.note: a saddle is a rider's seat, and more than one makes it plural

indicators.note: start of keeps only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A horse rider's injury: a bone broken by a problem with saddles.
explanation.walkthrough: SEATS reversed is STAES, and P goes in after the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The stapes, or stirrup, is the small bone of the middle ear, named for its stirrup shape.

clue.text: You'll be shocked with lunch (odd bits only) — outrageous

indicators.note: being shocked throws things into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: odd bits only keeps the first, third and fifth letters of the word

parts.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: A warning that the lunch on offer, served in scraps, is scandalous.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'll of You'll is just the link to be shocked; YOU plus three letters of lunch rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Unholy is an informal intensifier for something dreadful or outrageous, as in an unholy row.

clue.text: Patches bearing plumes Private dressed early

parts.note: Pte is the abbreviation for the army rank of private

indicators.note: to dress something is to arrange it, so the word's letters are set out anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier puts on his plumed patches before dawn parade.
explanation.walkthrough: Private looks like an adjective but is the soldier's rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Pterylae are the tracts of a bird's skin from which feathers grow, the feathered patches.

clue.text: Handle inlaid with iron found in Scottish temple,…

indicators.note: something inlaid with a material has that material set into its body

parts.note: a haft is the handle of a knife or axe
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A knife handle studded with iron turns up in a Scottish place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temple' looks like a building but is the side of the head, here in its Scots dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Haffet is a Scots dialect word for the side of the head, the temple.

clue.text: Electrical unit distorted when stripped of casing?

indicators.note: stripping off a casing removes the outside, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a thing tampered with has been interfered with and distorted

explanation.surface: A faulty electrical part has been damaged by having its cover removed.
explanation.walkthrough: TAMPERED loses its T and D.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere, or amp, is the SI unit of electric current.

clue.text: Bats? One such was affected emotionally

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bat or batt is a sheet of wadding, and this pressed fabric is one such material

explanation.walkthrough: Bats suggests cricket or flying mammals; Chambers gives bat (batt) as a sheet of felt or cotton wadding.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt is both a matted fabric used in sheets and the past tense of feel, to be touched emotionally.

clue.text: Former lover in France, Gaston's love, dead

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
a Frenchman's word for nothing, which love means in tennis
d is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's old flame, his great love, has died.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaston stands for any Frenchman, so his love, nil, is rien. Former marks the old sense of friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Friend once meant a lover or sweetheart, a sense now archaic, so a lover of former times.

clue.text: Expel some of college's tearaways

indicators.note: some of means only a run of letters from the words that follow is wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A college throws out some of its unruly students.
explanation.definitionFit: To egest is to discharge waste from the body, to expel it.

clue.text: Little pig in extremely messy sty twice consuming most of timber

indicators.note: twice says the jumbled pen word is used two times over in the build

parts.note: too means excessively, extremely

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the doubled piece takes the timber word between its halves

parts.note: the first use of the jumbled word

indicators.note: something messy is in disorder, so the letters of sty are jumbled
most of drops the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: timber is wood
twice: the jumbled word used again

explanation.surface: A piglet in a filthy pen, wallowing among bits of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: The little pig is a toe, from the nursery rhyme This little piggy; the twin jumbled sty sits either side of WOO (wood cut short).
explanation.definitionFit: Tootsy-wootsy is a child's word for a foot or toe, and toes are the little pigs of the nursery rhyme.

clue.text: … Half of which rang out thrillingly in part of Latin hymn (10, two words)

parts.words: Half of which rang out thrillingly
parts.note: surface reading: a bell or trumpet sounding out excitingly
setter's reading: the closing verses of Aquinas's eucharistic hymn, sung on their own at Benediction

explanation.surface: Continuing 6, half of a Scottish temple rings out with a thrilling sound during a Latin hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the plain anchor; the opening words are a loose cryptic hint at the well-known sung section rather than a letter-by-letter build.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantum Ergo is the name given to the final two stanzas of Pange Lingua, a Latin hymn by Thomas Aquinas.

clue.text: Breath tube, the one motorists must fill?

parts.note: plain reading: the airway from throat to lungs
surface reading: the tube a motorist blows into at a roadside breath test

explanation.surface: A roadside breath test, where the driver must fill the tube.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: every motorist blowing into a breathalyser fills their own windpipe first.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the windpipe, the tube that carries breath to the lungs.

clue.text: Carried like e.g. US babies in belt with soft lining

indicators.note: a lining sits inside, so the soft item goes within the word for belt

parts.note: to belt someone is to hit them
p (piano) means soft in music

explanation.surface: American babies get carried in a soft-lined belt sling.
explanation.walkthrough: HIT lined with P gives HIPT, a Chambers form of hipped: American mothers famously carry babies on the hip.
explanation.definitionFit: Hipt means carried on the hip, as American parents are said to carry infants.

clue.text: Have deep aversion for some French oral perhaps

parts.note: de is the French partitive, as in some bread
an oral is a spoken examination, one kind of test

explanation.surface: A student loathes part of their French oral exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe, to feel a deep dislike for something.

clue.text: Concealed connection run from van? (8, two words)

parts.note: to fly is to run away, to flee
the van, short for vanguard, is the front

explanation.surface: A hidden cable runs out of a delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: Van looks like a vehicle but is the leading part of an army; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly front is a strip of cloth covering the fastening of a garment, so the join is hidden.

clue.text: Damaged leaf holds elation up — it lacks links to other texts (8, two words)

definitions.text: it lacks links to other texts

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for elation reads bottom to top
holds means the jumbled word goes around the next piece
a damaged thing is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a lift is a boost of spirits, elation

explanation.surface: A torn page contains a joyful message but no references to other documents.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing a flat file is a plain data file with no structured links or relations to other files.

clue.text: Name a spot that's unpleasant

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for name
taken as written
a sty or stye is an inflamed spot on the eyelid

explanation.surface: Pointing out a place that is grim.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and unpleasant are ordinary synonyms for something disagreeable.

clue.text: Portraitist clothes wife alongside duke in blue fashion

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it round, so the painter's name goes outside

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely, court painter to Charles II
W is the abbreviation for wife
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A society painter dresses a wife beside a duke in a blue outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: W and D sit side by side, and LELY wraps round the pair. Blue here means smutty, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means indecent, so doing something in a blue way is doing it lewdly.

clue.text: What law or English schools will bag first in Greats — first or second? (7, two words)

indicators.note: to school something is to train it into a new shape, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: first in keeps only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Which Oxford faculty, law or English, will hand out a first or a second in Greats?
explanation.walkthrough: Greats is Oxford's classics degree, and first and second are degree classes; in fact they are a car's bottom gears. The G is held among the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: First and second are the low gears of a car, used for starting off and climbing.

clue.text: Brain tumour maybe cut from seraglio maiden

indicators.note: cut from says the letters are sliced out of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A harem girl has a medical diagnosis.
explanation.definitionFit: A glioma is a tumour arising from the supporting tissue of the brain or spine; maybe marks it as one kind.

clue.text: Perfume ingredient that is about reverse of failure

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation goes around the next piece

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read backwards

parts.note: a no-no is a flop or failure

explanation.surface: A perfumer describes an ingredient that rescues a failed scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionone is an aromatic compound with a violet scent, used in making perfumes.

clue.text: Emolliate dosage that's lethal in air

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation goes inside the word meaning air

parts.note: a person's air, their manner or bearing, is their mien
LD is the abbreviation for lethal dose

explanation.surface: Diluting a dose that would be fatal if released into the atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: Air means bearing, not the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: To emolliate is to soften, and to milden is to make milder, so both mean to soften.

clue.text: Spicy Asian dish: you'll find a mixture of types near the equator

parts.note: pi or pie is printers' jumbled type
places near the equator lie at low latitudes

explanation.surface: A curry recipe notes that a blend of spices is grown in the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: Types means printing type, not sorts. PILOW is a Chambers spelling of pilau.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilow is a variant spelling of pilau, spiced rice cooked in stock, a dish from South Asia and the Middle East.

clue.text: Fool taken in by devious imp, all over the place

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside the next piece
devious means winding and crooked, so the following word's letters are twisted round

parts.note: taken as written
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool is tricked by a scheming sprite and sent all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged imp splits round the fool; passim is the Latin word seen in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Passim is Latin for here and there, used in references to mean throughout a text, that is, everywhere.

clue.text: Sudden aggressive move by fencers inhibits love for leisurely stroll

indicators.note: to inhibit is to hold something in, so the next piece goes inside

parts.note: a lunge is the fencer's forward thrust
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A fencer's attack is held back to allow a gentle walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge is a lazy saunter, as a verb to loll or stroll idly.

clue.text: Company's succeeded with repackaging of Coalite

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

indicators.note: repackaging puts the contents in a new form, so the brand name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: Coalite is a British brand of smokeless fuel

explanation.surface: A fuel firm does well after relaunching its Coalite brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company's' looks like a firm's; read it as belonging to company in the sense of society. All eight letters, the S included, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Company can mean society, people in general, so of company is societal.

clue.text: Any old tat I'll leave for artist in making set of clothes?

indicators.note: the letter I departs and the next piece takes its place

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a suit is a matching set of clothes

explanation.surface: Old rags will do for an artist to make an outfit from.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist. Surat, named after the Indian port, is coarse cotton, and Chambers extends it to anything inferior.
explanation.definitionFit: Surat was a cheap cotton cloth, and the word came to mean anything of poor quality, mere tat.

clue.text: Sot, losing head, left without foot in crease

indicators.note: losing its head means the word for sot drops its first letter
without says the following abbreviation is taken out of the word

parts.note: a sot is a drunk
taken as written
ft is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: A drunk, falling over, ends up left lying in a crumpled heap.
explanation.walkthrough: DRUNK loses its D; LEFT loses FT. Runkle is a Scots and dialect word for a wrinkle.
explanation.definitionFit: A runkle is a crease or wrinkle, as in crumpled cloth.

clue.text: Judge, upwardly mobile post in India one's after

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving upwards means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: dak is the Indian word for the post or mail
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An ambitious judge, climbing the ranks, goes after a post in India.
explanation.walkthrough: One's after means I follows; the reversed DAK comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A kadi, or cadi, is a judge in a Muslim country who rules on Islamic law.

clue.text: Skirt with nothing on? That'll do for novelist

indicators.note: with means the next piece is added on, so the two words join end to end

parts.note: to hug a coast is to skirt it closely
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A skirt worn over nothing would suit a racy writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Skirt is a verb here, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo, author of Les Misérables, is a famous French novelist.

clue.text: The fins may be tangled in what's this

definitions.text: The fins may be tangled in what's this

indicators.note: tangled things are twisted out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A riddle: what is the thing a fish's fins get caught up in?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the letters of the first two words rearrange to the very thing that tangles fins.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishnet is a net for catching fish, in which their fins become entangled.

clue.text: A couple of food fish for shore wader

parts.note: first fish: the sander or zander, the pikeperch
second fish: the ling, a cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Two edible fish make a meal for a bird on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies both fish, eaten one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The sanderling is a small sandpiper that runs along the tideline, a wading bird of beaches.

clue.text: Rick and Gertrude? They're raised in cellar abroad maybe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the TV chef Rick Stein and the writer Gertrude Stein share a surname

definitions.text: They're raised in cellar abroad maybe
definitions.meaning: second meaning: beer mugs lifted in a German beer cellar

explanation.surface: Two famous people, a chef and a writer, grew up in a foreign basement.
explanation.walkthrough: Raised means lifted to drink, not brought up; the cellar abroad is a German Bierkeller.
explanation.definitionFit: Steins are large German beer mugs, and the plural of a surname shared by two people.

clue.text: Politician in grip of weird power

indicators.note: held in the grip of something means enclosed by it

parts.note: eery is a variant spelling of eerie
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is caught up in some strange force.
explanation.walkthrough: Eery is a Chambers variant spelling of eerie, and empery is an archaic literary word.
explanation.definitionFit: Empery is an old word for dominion or absolute rule, that is, power.
